messages:
Taylor: FYI, taking over night bridge at 23:00 UTC. current open alerts: kv-cache eviction surge in eu-west, embeddings queue growth in us-east, and increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate.
Jamal: noted — I'm secondary for the first 2 hours, can take paging if customer-impacting.
Sophia: I'm around until 00:30 UTC for handoff questions.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: kv-cache-evictions-eu-west increased to 120/min (threshold 30/min) — triggered at 22:42 UTC.
Taylor: Summary of what happened: after a small autoscaler hiccup we saw sustained KV evictions on the shared prefix cache. Priority: embedding requests are seeing tail latency > 2s. impact: some customers in EU reporting failed embedding jobs and slow chat responses.
Jamal: any customers currently paged?
Taylor: Not paged yet — still investigating severity. If we see retries/backlog > 5m we'll escalate.
Sophia: Quick runbook pointers: playbook -> `runbooks/kv-cache-eviction`. TL;DR: 1) reduce prefix eviction pressure by disabling noncritical prefetch; 2) increase cache max size for eu-west pool; 3) if that fails, enable routing-fallback to dedicated embeddings pool.
Taylor: Actions in progress: 
- ran `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep eu-west` to confirm pod count (pods healthy).
- bumped config: `runtime.cache.max_prefix_mb=1024 -> 1536` for eu-west group on the config server (APPLY in progress).
- paused prefetch worker group `prefetch-worker-3` via `infra-cli scale --service prefetch-worker-3 --replicas 0` (paused to reduce churn).
Jamal: Good. Monitoring dashboard shows sustained drop in eviction rate since the scale down ~2m ago, but embeddings queue still up ~400 items.
incident-bot: Metric note: embeddings-queue-length-us-east = 412 (baseline 20).
Taylor: Mitigation step queued: 1) increase embeddings routing to fallback pool (routing weight change) for low-priority customers to reduce us-east backlog. 2) schedule a short dedicated-burst on eu-west (10m) if eviction rate stays >50/min.
Sophia: If we enable routing-fallback, I'll update the routing policy to send non-SLA traffic to `embeddings-fallback-1`. Command: `routerctl set-weight --route embeddings --region eu-west --target embeddings-fallback-1 --weight 0.25` (will do if Taylor gives thumbs).
Taylor: Go ahead when ready. Noting to log change in rollout-trace: run `rolloutctl annotate 2487654321 "fallback 25% for non-sla"`.
Jamal: I'll start a short canary of the routing change and watch request success rate. If 5xxs increase, roll back immediately.
Taylor: Also enabling increased prewarming for the fallback pool to reduce cold-start tail latency. kicked `infra-cli prewarm --pool embeddings-fallback-1 --count 6`.
Sophia: Customer-impact assessment: currently approx 2% of embedding requests in EU see timeouts; 10% of low-priority batched jobs delayed >60s. No major customer escalations yet but support queue has two tickets (internal IDs: S-7891, S-7892).
Jamal: Paging decision: I'll page if the number of failed jobs > 20 or SLO violation > 10% for > 10min.
Taylor: Agreed. Also note that the /v1/generate 5xx spike seems correlated with a single model shard in us-east. I've put that shard in maintenance mode: `shardctl drain --shard-id shard-42-us-east`.
incident-bot: Action log: config change applied by Taylor at 23:06 UTC; prefetch worker paused at 23:07 UTC; prewarm triggered at 23:08 UTC.
Taylor: Current ask for night team: 
- Jamal: own paging threshold and be ready to escalate to infra if routing changes fail.
- Sophia: hold the runbook link and help coordinate customer comms if we need to page.
- Me (Taylor): I'll follow the eviction metric and decide on burst capacity by 23:20 UTC.
Jamal: I'll keep a watch on SLO dashboard and embeddings-queue length. If queue doesn't drop below 100 in 15m, I'll trigger fallback 50% and page infra.
Sophia: Noted. I'll draft a short customer update template we can send to affected customers if we escalate.
Taylor: Any known gaps? We don't have a dedicated on-prem tech on call this shift; if the escalation requires HSM access we may need to call in ops. That gap is noted for leadership.
Jamal: Acknowledged — I'll include that in the bridge update at 23:15 UTC.
incident-bot: Reminder: runbook checkpoint due at 23:20 UTC.
Taylor: Handoff plan for next shift (ETA 01:00 UTC): capture final metrics, list any rolling changes, and whether burst capacity was used. If we're still in mitigation, hand off primary to next oncall (Avery).
Sophia: I'll stay available for 30 more minutes to help with any routing rollbacks.
Jamal: switching to active monitoring, ping me in thread with new graphs.
Taylor: Thanks team — I'll post a short summary at 23:20 UTC with decisions. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Thread archived for followups; continue replies here for the handoff.
